text:
maria: Heads-up — after the driver upgrade to CUDA 12.x on the h100 pool we are seeing a p99 token-latency regression for long-sequence workloads (>=768).

alex: Seeing the same in the canary traces. p50 is fine, p99 up ~2.3x for seq 1024. Throughput drop on the dedicated hosts too.

jia: Posted profiler samples. Kernel selection looks different — autotuner is preferring matmul_fused_v3 for long seqs now but matmul_v2 was faster previously. Suspect a change in driver heuristics or cuBLAS behavior affecting our heuristic scoring.

maria: Logs from one request (snippet):
```
[2026-03-10T12:02:45Z] kernel_pick: model=redwood-v2, seq=1024, arch=h100, candidate=[matmul_v2, matmul_fused_v3, matmul_tile8], scores=[14.2, 9.1, 12.6], chosen=matmul_fused_v3
[2026-03-10T12:02:45Z] runtime_exec: kernel=matmul_fused_v3, latency_ms=3.21 (per-token)
[2026-03-10T12:02:45Z] runtime_exec: kernel=matmul_v2 (re-run], latency_ms=1.38
```

alex: That second line where matmul_v2 has ~1.4ms but wasn't chosen is the problem. Autotuner scoring moved weights. I can repro locally with driver 555 and not with 535.

jia: benchbot results:
```
benchbot: h100 driver=555, seq=1024, batch=1 -> matmul_fused_v3: 3.2ms, matmul_v2: 1.4ms
benchbot: h100 driver=535, seq=1024, batch=1 -> matmul_v2: 1.3ms, matmul_fused_v3: 2.9ms
```

ops-bot: Reported incident to infra, created ticket INF-4123.

maria: Short-term mitigation options? Pin drivers back, force kernel override for long sequences, or tweak autotuner to emphasize empirical latency traces more.

alex: Recommend immediate rollback on 20% of canary nodes to driver 535 to validate. If rollback restores p99 we can schedule fleet-wide rollback during low traffic window.

jia: I pushed a small autotuner hotfix that increases weight of observed latency by 2x for the next scoring window — it's in staging but I don't want to promote until we validate telemetry. It reduces bad picks in our tests.

maria: Plan: 1) roll 20% canary back to driver 535 (infra) 2) run benchbot sweep for seq 256/512/1024 3) enable autotuner hotfix in canary if bench looks good 4) coordinate rollback/rollforward decision.

alex: Infra rollback command we used in canary (example):
```bash
# ssh to node
sudo systemctl stop inference-node
sudo apt-get install --allow-downgrades -y nvidia-driver-535=535.108.05
sudo reboot
```

ops-bot: Canary rollback scheduled at 2026-03-10T18:00Z on: infra-canary-1, infra-canary-2. Notifying oncall.

jia: Also saw KV cache miss amplification in long seqs after driver change — more time spent on KV cache loads with the fused kernel. Might be memory access pattern differences. We'll add KV probe metrics to trace to confirm.

maria: Good catch. Add kv_cache.load_ms to the canary traces and tag by kernel_name.

alex: If rollback fixes both kernel picks and KV latency, we declare driver 555 incompatible and block upgrade until vendor patch or we adapt heuristics. 

maria: Post-mortem action items: update autotuner to include driver-version in features, add a quick canary perf-check in driver rollouts, and add an auto-rollback hook when p99 regressions >20% for 30min.

jia: I'll open PRs: autotuner driver feature + kv metrics + hotfix toggle.

alex: I'll coordinate rollback window with infra and schedule a short post-rollback validation run.

maria: Thanks — keep updates here. :thumbsup:

benchbot: Full bench sweep completed on canary-rollback nodes: driver=535 -> p99 token-latency restored to baseline for seq=1024, throughput +18%.

maria: Closing loop — infra proceed with fleet rollback this evening and ops will block future driver 555 rollouts until next vendor revision or we land autotuner + KV patches.

ops-bot: INF-4123 updated: status=rolling-back, rollout_eta=2026-03-10T23:00Z.
